claims: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed flight test.
Artemis II launched on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II sends four astronauts around the Moon and back.
Artemis II marks the first human deep-space mission since 1972.
Artemis II uses the SLS rocket.
Artemis II uses the Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II tests critical life-support systems.
Artemis II crew includes NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II verifies Orion’s systems including manual piloting and radiation shielding.
Artemis II travels over 4,000 miles past the Moon's far side.
Victor Glover will be the first person of color to travel to the vicinity of the Moon.
Christina Koch will be the first woman to travel to the vicinity of the Moon.
Jeremy Hansen will be the first non-U.S. citizen to travel to the vicinity of the Moon.
Artemis II launched from Kennedy Space Center.
Artemis II crew conducts orbital maneuvers before performing the Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI).
Artemis II crew performs Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI) to head to the Moon.
Artemis II crew separates from the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS).
Artemis II crew practices docking maneuvers.
Orion spacecraft circles the Moon.
Artemis II reaches distances up to 4,700 miles beyond the lunar surface.
Artemis II follows a free-return trajectory.
Orion capsule is named Integrity.
Orion capsule reenters Earth's atmosphere at speeds of about 25,000 mph.
Artemis II has planned splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
Artemis III is scheduled for 2027 or later.
Artemis III aims to land astronauts at the Moon's South Pole.
